[ASSISTANT_SAID] The `\documentclass{article}` command is used to specify the type of document in LaTeX, affecting the default layout and behavior.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The `article` document class is designed for short documents such as articles, reports, and small books.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The `\documentclass{article}` command does not take any optional arguments by default, but optional arguments can be passed using square brackets.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Common optional arguments for the `article` document class include: `10pt`, `11pt`, or `12pt` for font size; `letterpaper`, `a4paper`, or other paper sizes; `twocolumn` for two-column typesetting; `landscape` for landscape orientation; and `titlepage` for a separate title page.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Example of setting font size to `12pt`, paper size to `a4paper`, and typesetting in two columns: `\documentclass[12pt,a4paper,twocolumn]{article}`.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some optional arguments may not be compatible with each other or with certain packages or document layouts.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Provided a LaTeX template for the `pgfplots` package to graph 4 graphs on the same set of axes with points on each graph.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The template includes a `tikzpicture` environment and an `axis` environment for drawing graphs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The `axis` environment options include width, height, axis lines, labels, tick marks, grid options, and limits.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The `addplot` commands are used to add plots to the graph, specifying colors and coordinates for points.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] The initial template plots points at coordinates: (1,2), (-1,-2), (-1,2), and (1,-2) in different quadrants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Added a legend to the previous code with entries for each of the four graphs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The legend is positioned below the plot area with two columns and smaller font size.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Each `addplot` command for the graphs includes a `label` option for the legend.
